summary: Johannes Jung, or John Young, of Easton, Pennsylvania, father of Mary Young Croup; John's 6th-great-grandfather, though the line is not yet proven.
bio: John Young, or Johannes Jung, of Easton, Northampton County, Pennsylvania, was the father of Mary Young, who married Frederick Croup, and so is John's 6th-great-grandfather, though the connection has not yet been proven from records. Family records give his dates as 19 December 1751 to 6 May 1813, but those are the same dates given for his wife, Anna Maria Doll, and may really be hers. Another account makes him a man born about 1745 who had died before September 1787, leaving his widow Maria and ten children: Maria, born in January 1776, who became the wife of Frederick Grub; Sara; Johannes; Susannah; Peter; Catherine; Elizabeth; Henry; Jacob; and Margaretha. He was not the John Young of Hanover Township who appears in Plumb's history as an associate of the Stewarts from Paxtang in the 1770s.

researchNotes:
The tree shows John Young Sr (1751-1813), with a document image, as father of Mary Young. 'Young' is too common in Northampton County to resolve online, and both he and his wife carry identical 1751-1813 dates. Lead (speculative): a 'Johannes Young/Jung' heads both lists of the 1754 Phoenix, the same ship as Andreas Grub; if he came from the Kusel area he could be the father of a John b. 1751 (then a 3-year-old, not listed by name). The Jettenbach Grubs had married Jungs for generations. Plumb's 1885 History of Hanover's John Young is a 1770s Paxtang/Lancaster 'Stewart associate', a different man. No SAR record for a John Young of Northampton was found.

The FamilySearch tree has an independent profile for Mary (Young) Croup's father: 'Johannes Jung', of Easton, born about 1745 and dead before 12 September 1787, husband of Anna Maria Doll (1751-1813), with ten children - Maria (Jan 1776, Mrs Frederick Grub), Sara (1777), Johannes (1781-1813), Susannah (1783), Peter (1784-1854), Catherine, Elizabeth, Henry, Jacob and Margaretha ([R4-S1]). Its only cited source is the will of 'Maria Young' in Northampton County Will Book 4, p.458 (presumably his widow's, 1813). If correct, Johnny's tree has given John Young his widow's death year: the tree's 1751-1813 dates for both spouses look like a copy, and the '12 Sep 1787' terminus suggests an administration or Orphans' Court date in Northampton County.
